title: The Wall Street Journal: ownership and voting control
summary: The Wall Street Journal is a US newspaper published by Dow Jones, part of News Corp. At June 30, 2026, LGC Holdco held approximately 34.52% of News Corp’s voting Class B shares. Lachlan Murdoch controls voting of that block through an appointed managing director. No subsequent sale of the publication was identified.

nodes.name: The Wall Street Journal
nodes.description: US newspaper and digital news publication based in New York, covering business, finance, economics and general news.
nodes.endpointNote: Publishing relationship traced to Dow Jones.

nodes.name: Dow Jones & Company, Inc.
nodes.description: Publisher of The Wall Street Journal and a business within News Corp.
nodes.endpointNote: Corporate parent identified as News Corp; intermediate legal holding entities were not established.

nodes.name: News Corporation
nodes.description: Publicly traded US media and information services group, operating as News Corp. Its dual-class structure separates ordinary voting rights from much of its equity.
nodes.endpointNote: Significant shareholding and associated voting control traced separately; other shareholders are not comprehensively mapped.

nodes.name: LGC Holdco, LLC
nodes.description: Delaware company holding News Corp shares formerly held by the Murdoch Family Trust. Owned by the LGC Family Trusts.
nodes.endpointNote: Third relationship level reached. Underlying family trusts and the manager structure are not expanded.

nodes.name: Lachlan K. Murdoch
nodes.description: Controls voting and disposition of LGC Holdco’s News Corp shares through appointment and replacement of its manager’s managing director, subject to limited exceptions.
nodes.endpointNote: Individual stopping point. Voting authority does not establish personal economic ownership of the entire family shareholding.

edges.description: The publication’s official About page identifies Dow Jones as its publisher.

evidence.title: About Us - The Wall Street Journal
evidence.excerpt: Dow Jones & Co., a unit of News Corp, publishes The Wall Street Journal

edges.description: News Corp is identified as Dow Jones’s corporate parent. This edge represents the group relationship without asserting a verified direct equity percentage.

evidence.title: About Us - The Wall Street Journal

edges.description: Percentage refers exclusively to outstanding Class B common stock, the ordinary voting class, not total equity. LGC also held less than 1% of Class A stock. The annual report confirms the transfer from the former Murdoch Family Trust.

evidence.title: News Corporation — Form 10-K for the year ended June 30, 2026
evidence.excerpt: approximately 34.52% of the Company’s Class B Common Stock

edges.description: Indirect control of the LGC voting block, rather than a majority of all votes: Lachlan appoints and can replace the managing director who decides voting and disposition of LGC’s shares, subject to limited exceptions. He disclaims beneficial ownership. The family’s contractual 44% voting ceiling is a limit, not its actual holding.

evidence.title: News Corporation — Form 10-K for the year ended June 30, 2026
evidence.excerpt: appointed, and may be replaced, by Lachlan K. Murdoch

gaps: Research reflects public sources available through September 17, 2026; the latest verified shareholding observation is June 30, 2026.
News Corp’s remaining institutional and individual shareholders are not comprehensively mapped. Class B percentages must not be interpreted as percentages of total economic ownership.
The three-level limit stops the ownership branch at LGC Holdco. Its underlying trusts and manager are not separately graphed.
Intermediate legal holding companies between Dow Jones and News Corp, and current special editorial appointment arrangements, were not established.
The official About page is undated, so its relationship observation dates are null. Wikidata identifiers were not verified.
